text:
Aditi Sen: Hey team — just finished onboarding and Kandji says my MBP is enrolled, but Zoom and Google Meet can't access camera or screen-share. When I try to share screen it errors with "Screen Recording permission required" but I never got the macOS permission prompt. Any tips? macOS Ventura 13.5.1, M1 Pro.

rachel-it: Welcome! Can you check System Settings → Privacy & Security → Camera and Screen Recording? Sometimes the prompt gets suppressed and the app never shows up. Also check Accessibility for Zoom. If nothing there, paste the output of `profiles status -type enrollment` and `spctl --status`.

Aditi Sen: I checked — Camera and Screen Recording are NOT listed, Accessibility doesn't show Zoom either. `profiles status -type enrollment` returns: "Enrolled via Kandji (MDM)". `spctl --status` shows: "assessments enabled". Not sure how to force the prompt.

jake-devex: Heya — a couple ways to recover: (1) Try to re-trigger the TCC (privacy) prompt locally: run:

```
tccutil reset ScreenCapture com.zoom.us
# then reinstall Zoom from https://zoom.us/download
```

On macOS sometimes resetting the TCC DB and reinstalling the app will cause the permission dialog to reappear. (2) If reinstall is blocked by MDM restrictions, we can push a Kandji allowlist policy that grants Zoom the Screen Recording entitlement for company-managed machines. We avoid blanket approvals when possible for privacy reasons.

Aditi Sen: Running `tccutil reset ScreenCapture com.zoom.us` now... reinstalling Zoom... installer failed — it asked for admin and my account isn't admin so it couldn't complete. Still no prompt.

rachel-it: If the installer needs admin we can either (A) push the Kandji package/allowlist for you, or (B) grant a very short-lived temporary admin (ssh/sudo) so you can reinstall and trigger the prompt yourself. @people-ops can approve temporary admin. Adding @security-ops for visibility.

people-ops: @rachel-it please file a temp-admin request with duration 2 hours and reason "trigger screen recording TCC prompt for Zoom during onboarding". Approving once request is in the queue.

kandji-bot: Kandji policy "Zoom ScreenCapture Allowlist" queued to apply to device Aditi-Sen-MBP.

kandji-bot: Kandji policy applied successfully — 2026-03-23T14:12:03Z

rachel-it: Policy pushed. Aditi — can you reboot and try Zoom share again? If it still fails we can remote in during pairing.

Aditi Sen: Rebooted, tried share — the permission prompt finally appeared. Gave Screen Recording + Camera + Accessibility access to Zoom, and Google Meet now can use camera too. Everything works now, thank you!! :tada:

security-ops: Noted — policy allowlist limited to company-managed images and only for the Zoom bundle ID. If you see any unexpected permission prompts for apps you didn't install, ping us immediately.

jake-devex: Awesome. I'll create a short KB for new hires: "If TCC prompt missing on macOS: try `tccutil reset` + reinstall, otherwise request Kandji allowlist or temp admin."

Aditi Sen: One last Q — does giving Zoom Accessibility/Screen Recording let it log keystrokes or read my passwords? :slightly_frowning_face:

security-ops: Short answer: Zoom Accessibility is to allow screen sharing and remote control; it does not, by itself, enable generic keylogging. Company policy restricts which apps we allow to have these entitlements. If you want an extra check we can run a quick endpoint review on your device.

Aditi Sen: Great, thanks everyone — saved my pairing session.

rachel-it: Glad it's sorted. Tag us in #help if anything else pops up during first-week setup.

Aditi Sen: Will do, thanks again! :wave:
